description: Figma markets AI features for product design and prototyping.
fact_1: Figma says users can prompt to code with AI in Figma Make.
fact_2: Figma First Draft can transform ideas into editable wireframes or designs.

description: Uizard markets itself as AI-powered UI design software for product teams.
fact_1: Uizard describes its UI design as powered by AI.
fact_2: Uizard Autodesigner generates multi-screen mockups from text prompts.

description: Framer includes AI-assisted website design features relevant to UI design workflows.
fact_1: Framer says AI can generate site layouts and advanced components in seconds.
fact_2: Framer positions itself as a no-code site builder used by designers.

description: Visily is an AI UI design tool for app and website interfaces.
fact_1: Visily says it can generate UI designs from text prompts.
fact_2: Visily says it can turn screenshots and sketches into editable designs.

description: Relume markets AI-assisted website planning and wireframing for design workflows.
fact_1: Relume says it generates sitemaps, wireframes, and style guides with AI.
fact_2: Relume says generated components can be exported to Figma, Webflow, or React.

description: Miro offers AI features for UX and UI design collaboration.
fact_1: Miro says its AI wireframe generator turns text descriptions into editable wireframes.
fact_2: Miro says its AI UI design tools can generate components and complete app screens.

description: Maze markets AI-powered product research capabilities.
fact_1: Maze describes its offering as AI-powered product research.
fact_2: Maze states it uses OpenAI for text and Rev AI for voice in AI features.

description: Dovetail markets AI features for customer and UX research workflows.
fact_1: Dovetail says its AI centralizes and analyzes customer data.
fact_2: Dovetail announced AI Agents and AI Docs capabilities.

description: UX Pilot markets an AI UI generator for rapid interface design.
fact_1: UX Pilot says its AI generates UI designs and screen flows from prompts.
fact_2: UX Pilot says users can transfer outputs to Figma and export production-ready code.

description: Builder.io markets AI-powered Figma-to-code conversion for UI implementation.
fact_1: Builder.io labels Visual Copilot as AI-powered Figma to code.
fact_2: Builder.io says it outputs code for frameworks including React, Qwik, Angular, Kotlin, and Flutter.

description: Locofy markets AI-assisted design-to-code tooling.
fact_1: Locofy describes itself as an AI-powered design-to-code tool.
fact_2: Locofy says it uses in-house Large Design Models for Figma-to-React conversion.

description: v0 markets AI-based generation of apps and websites from prompts.
fact_1: v0 says users can generate working applications in minutes with AI.
fact_2: v0 Model API supports text and image inputs and is labeled multimodal.

description: Dora AI markets prompt-based website generation.
fact_1: Dora AI says it generates sites from prompts and provides an end-to-end AI pipeline.
fact_2: Dora AI says sites are generated from copy to composition without predefined templates.

description: Lunacy includes AI capabilities in a UI/UX design tool.
fact_1: Lunacy pages describe AI-powered capabilities for UI/UX work.
fact_2: Lunacy is presented as a UI/UX design tool with built-in graphic assets and AI tools.

description: Hotjar includes AI-assisted capabilities relevant to UX research and feedback analysis.
fact_1: Hotjar documentation lists AI survey creation, AI survey summaries, and survey sentiment analysis.
fact_2: Hotjar describes itself as a product experience insights platform for behavior analytics and feedback.

description: UserTesting markets AI-powered experience research capabilities.
fact_1: UserTesting AI is described as AI-powered support for recruitment, test planning, feedback collection, and analysis.
fact_2: UserTesting states AI Insight Summary is GPT-powered.

description: Looppanel positions itself as AI-assisted UX research analysis and repository software.
fact_1: Looppanel says its purpose-built AI reduces manual tagging and accelerates analysis.
fact_2: Looppanel says it provides a research repository to find answers across customer research sources.

description: Marvin markets AI assistance for research synthesis.
fact_1: Marvin Ask AI is described as giving instant data-backed answers from research.
fact_2: Marvin says users can search, analyze, and synthesize research data with Marvin AI.

description: Notably markets AI-powered qualitative research synthesis.
fact_1: Notably says it helps teams turn qualitative data into insights with AI.
fact_2: Notably describes its repository feature as an AI-powered research repository.

description: Attention Insight markets AI-based pre-launch design analytics.
fact_1: Attention Insight describes itself as an AI-powered analytics tool that generates attention metrics and heatmaps.
fact_2: Attention Insight says it uses deep learning algorithms to simulate human vision.

description: Lyssna combines UX research workflows with AI-assisted synthesis features.
fact_1: Lyssna analysis features include AI-powered summaries.
fact_2: Lyssna describes itself as a remote user research platform for moderated and unmoderated studies.

description: Condens markets AI features tailored for UX research analysis.
fact_1: Condens describes Condens AI as purpose-built for UX research.
fact_2: Condens says it provides AI-powered transcription and summarization capabilities.

description: Great Question includes AI features in its UX research platform.
fact_1: Great Question homepage includes a 'Start free study with AI' callout.
fact_2: Great Question help docs say Great Question AI supports synthesis, querying studies, and summaries.

description: Sprig markets AI-native research tooling for UX teams.
fact_1: Sprig homepage describes AI-native surveys and AI-powered study workflows.
fact_2: Sprig AI Insights says AI clusters responses and surfaces patterns and pain points in real time.

description: Ballpark markets AI-driven user research workflows.
fact_1: Ballpark homepage states 'Research anything. Powered by AI.'
fact_2: Ballpark says its AI interviewer adapts in real time and asks smart follow-up questions.
